panels.description:
**Uptime**

The amount of time since the last restart of the MySQL server process.
panels.title: Uptime

panels.description:
**Current QPS**

Based on the queries reported by MySQL's ``SHOW STATUS`` command, it is the number of statements executed by the server within the last second. This variable includes statements executed within stored programs, unlike the Questions variable. It does not count 
``COM_PING`` or ``COM_STATISTICS`` commands.
panels.title: Current QPS

panels.description:
**InnoDB Buffer Pool Size**

InnoDB maintains a storage area called the buffer pool for caching data and indexes in memory.  Knowing how the InnoDB buffer pool works, and taking advantage of it to keep frequently accessed data in memory, is one of the most important aspects of MySQL tuning. The goal is to keep the working set in memory. In most cases, this should be between 60%-90% of available memory on a dedicated database host, but depends on many factors.

links.title: Tuning the InnoDB Buffer Pool Size

panels.title: InnoDB Buffer Pool

panels.description:
**Max Connections** 

Max Connections is the maximum permitted number of simultaneous client connections. By default, this is 151. Increasing this value increases the number of file descriptors that mysqld requires. If the required number of descriptors are not available, the server reduces the value of Max Connections.

mysqld actually permits Max Connections + 1 clients to connect. The extra connection is reserved for use by accounts that have the SUPER privilege, such as root.

Max Used Connections is the maximum number of connections that have been in use simultaneously since the server started.

Connections is the number of connection attempts (successful or not) to the MySQL server.
panels.title: MySQL Connections

panels.description:
**MySQL Questions**

The number of statements executed by the server. This includes only statements sent to the server by clients and not statements executed within stored programs, unlike the Queries used in the QPS calculation. 

This variable does not count the following commands:
* ``COM_PING``
* ``COM_STATISTICS``
* ``COM_STMT_PREPARE``
* ``COM_STMT_CLOSE``
* ``COM_STMT_RESET``
panels.title: MySQL Questions

panels.description:
**MySQL Active Threads**

Threads Connected is the number of open connections, while Threads Running is the number of threads not sleeping.
panels.title: MySQL Client Thread Activity

panels.description:
**MySQL Thread Cache**

The thread_cache_size variable sets how many threads the server should cache to reuse. When a client disconnects, the client's threads are put in the cache if the cache is not full. It is autosized in MySQL 5.6.8 and above (capped to 100). Requests for threads are satisfied by reusing threads taken from the cache if possible, and only when the cache is empty is a new thread created.

* *Threads_created*: The number of threads created to handle connections.
* *Threads_cached*: The number of threads in the thread cache.
panels.title: MySQL Thread Cache

panels.description: Percentage of InnoDB buffer pool read requests that are served from memory instead of disk. Higher values indicate better buffer pool utilization
panels.title: MySQL Buffer Pool Efficiency

panels.description: Shows the InnoDB storage engine disk activity, including the number of data pages read from disk (Data Reads) and written to disk (Data Writes) for the selected MySQL instance.
panels.title: MySQL InnoDB Data Reads/Writes

panels.description: Shows the rate of InnoDB log waits and OS-level fsync operations for the selected MySQL instance.
panels.title: MySQL InnoDB Log Waits & Fsyncs (Rate)

panels.description: Rate of reads and read requests in the InnoDB buffer pool per second.
panels.title: MySQL Buffer Pool Activity

panels.description: The rate of time (in milliseconds per second) spent acquiring row locks in InnoDB. High values may indicate contention or locking issues in the database.
panels.title: MySQL Row Lock Time

panels.description: The rate of row lock waits in InnoDB per second. Higher values may indicate lock contention.
panels.title: MySQL Row Lock Waits

panels.description: The average time (in milliseconds) InnoDB spends waiting for row locks per lock wait. Higher values indicate longer contention times.
panels.title: MySQL Avg Row Lock Wait Time

panels.description: The rate at which table locks were granted immediately without waiting. A consistently high value indicates low contention.
panels.title: MySQL Table Locks

panels.description: Displays the rate at which table locks required waiting before being granted. Higher values may indicate lock contention or concurrency bottlenecks.
panels.title: MySQL Table Lock Waits

panels.description: Displays the rate of slow queries detected by MySQL over time.
panels.title: MySQL Slow Queries

panels.description: Displays the rate of SQL statement errors over time. A high rate may indicate query or schema issues.
panels.title: MySQL Error Quries

panels.description:
Displays the rate of queries executed without using an index, as reported by MySQL Performance Schema.
A consistently high value may indicate missing indexes or inefficient query plans that can degrade performance.
panels.title: MySQL No Index Used Queries

panels.description:
Displays the rate of temporary objects created by MySQL during query execution.
A high number of disk-based temporary tables or files may indicate insufficient memory settings or inefficient query design.
panels.title: MySQL Temporary Objects

panels.description: Displays the rate of different types of SELECT operations executed by MySQL, providing insights into query efficiency and index usage patterns. A high rate of full joins or full table scans may indicate missing indexes or inefficient query design.
panels.title: MySQL Select Types

panels.description:
Monitors MySQL network throughput, showing the rate of bytes received from and sent to clients.
A sudden increase in network traffic may indicate heavy query loads, large result sets, or inefficient data transfer patterns.
panels.title: MySQL Network Traffic

panels.description:
Displays key memory components used internally by MySQL and InnoDB, such as buffer pools, caches, and adaptive hash memory.
These metrics help identify memory usage distribution across different MySQL subsystems, useful for tuning memory parameters and identifying potential bottlenecks.
panels.title: MySQL Internal Memory Overview

panels.description:
Displays the top 5 MySQL command types executed per second.
Helps identify workload patterns and detect unusual query activity (e.g., frequent commits or rollbacks).
panels.title: Top Command Counters

panels.description: Displays MySQL internal handler operations to understand how queries access tables and indexes. A high number of Handler_read_rnd_next may indicate full table scans or missing indexes.
panels.title: MySQL Handlers

panels.description:
Displays the rate of internal transaction-related handler operations such as COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT, and PREPARE.
Helps identify transaction workload patterns and detect abnormal rollback spikes.
panels.title: MySQL Transaction Handlers

panels.description:
Displays the number of MySQL threads per state (Sleep, Query, Locked, etc.) over time.
Helps identify connection saturation, long-running queries, and locking issues.
panels.title: Process States

panels.description: Shows the top 5 MySQL thread states by average number of threads observed in the past hour. Useful for identifying which operations are most common or blocking database resources.
panels.title: Top Process States Hourly

panels.description: Shows the number of files opened per second by the MySQL server, helping detect sudden increases in file handling activity.
panels.title: MySQL File Openings

panels.description: Displays table open activity and the efficiency of the table open cache. Includes the number of tables opened, successful table cache hits, table cache misses, and cache overflows. Useful for understanding how well the table cache is utilized and identifying potential bottlenecks in table access.
panels.title: MySQL Table Open Cache Status

panels.description:
**MySQL Open Tables**

The recommendation is to set the `table_open_cache_instances` to a loose correlation to virtual CPUs, keeping in mind that more instances means the cache is split more times. If you have a cache set to 500 but it has 10 instances, each cache will only have 50 cached.

The `table_definition_cache` and `table_open_cache` can be left as default as they are auto-sized MySQL 5.6 and above (ie: do not set them to any value).
panels.title: MySQL Open Tables

panels.description: Displays the number of currently open table definitions, the maximum table definition cache size, and the rate of table definitions being opened. Helps monitor cache usage and detect potential cache pressure.
panels.title: MySQL Table Definition Cache
